title: Delegation status returns 404 for both an absent delegation and another parent's delegation
outcome:
The parent-scoped delegation endpoints answer "not found" and "not yours" with the same 404 and the same body text ("delegation not found"). The two facts need different responses from the caller: absent means the record is gone and the caller should stop waiting; out-of-scope means the delegation is alive and owned by another parent, and the caller should ask that parent.

OBSERVED, not theorised. Two sibling coordinator sessions share one repository. Session B spawned a read-only reviewer pair and announced the delegation ids over the mailbox. Session A, which did not own them, called the list endpoint and the status endpoint:
  - the list endpoint returned twenty delegations, all owned by A, and neither of B's;
  - the status endpoint returned 404 "delegation not found" for both of B's ids.
Both answers are correct under parent scoping and both are indistinguishable from the answers for a deleted delegation.

IMPACT AS IT ACTUALLY HAPPENED: session A concluded the reviewers were dead, and sent an urgent correction to a peer project retracting an earlier disclosure that two agents were loading the machine. The peer was at that moment entering a serialized benchmark window and had pre-committed to classifying any slowdown rather than attributing it to our reviewers. The false retraction handed them an exculpatory story for a load that was in fact real. The pair had in truth completed normally; the fan-in landed in session B four minutes later.

WHY THE CALLER CANNOT DEFEND AGAINST THIS: an instrument that answers "absent" when it means "outside your scope" gives a caller no way to detect that the question left its domain. A caller who has verified the instrument on twenty in-scope questions carries that trust into the twenty-first, which is a question of a different class. The failure is not inattention; it is that the API never says "I cannot see that".

FIX DIRECTION: separate the two cases at the boundary. 403/404 split, or one status with a machine-readable reason field distinguishing "unknown id" from "id belongs to another parent". Whichever is chosen, the message text must differ, because a human reader and a log both key on the text. A cheap partial improvement, if scope leakage is a concern: keep 404 but return a distinct reason code, since acknowledging the existence of an id the caller already possesses leaks nothing the caller does not already have.

RELATED SURFACE WORTH CHECKING IN THE SAME PASS: every other parent-scoped delegation route (result, cancel, follow-up, wait, resume) shares the same scoping predicate and very likely the same conflation.
